name: ratesonar
description: Dated record of the interest rates Australian banks and lenders advertise, plus RBA market curves. Read-only tools: find_products, compare_rates, rate_history, rate_details, rate_changes, list_series, series, bank_position, bank_analysis, yield_curve, curve_pipeline_status.

interface.longDescription:
RateSonar keeps a daily record of the interest rates that Australian banks and lenders advertise. Each rate carries the date RateSonar recorded it. The record starts on 12 June 2026.

Use RateSonar to:
- Compare current advertised rates across lenders for home loans, savings accounts, term deposits, credit cards, personal loans, car loans and business loans. Filter home loans by owner-occupied or investment, principal-and-interest or interest-only, and variable or fixed. Filter term deposits by term.
- See one product's advertised rate on each recorded day since 12 June 2026, and when it changed.
- Read one product's full published detail: rate tiers, bonus conditions, fees, eligibility and constraints, as the lender published them on a given date.
- List recent rate changes: rises, cuts, new products and withdrawn products, with the size of each move in basis points.
- Read standard series, such as the variable home loan rate minus the RBA cash rate, for each lender and as a market median.
- Place one bank's deposit and loan prices against comparable peers, its own history and the RBA cash rate, with an evidence-checked reading of that position.
- Read dated RBA market curves: bond yields and the RBA's fitted zero, forward and discount curves.

How the data works:
- Most rates come from the product reference data that Australian lenders publish under the Consumer Data Right (CDR). RateSonar also records the RBA cash rate and some lender web pages.
- RateSonar answers from its own stored record. It does not send your question to a lender.
- A day with no record is marked "carried-forward". Spreads and medians are marked "derived". Neither is shown as a new observation.
- RateSonar has no record before 12 June 2026.

Limits:
- RateSonar reports advertised rates. It gives no personal financial advice, does not say which product suits a person, takes no applications and moves no money.
- It covers Australian lenders only. A lender that does not publish CDR product data can be missing.
- Without an API key, series requests return the last 31 days.

Who it is for: people who compare Australian bank products, mortgage brokers, analysts, journalists and researchers who need a dated record of advertised rates.

No sign-in is needed to start. Every tool only reads data.
defaultPrompt: What is the highest 12-month term deposit rate in Australia right now?
Which lenders changed home loan rates in the last 7 days?
How has CBA's standard variable home loan rate changed since June 2026?

positive.description: Rank current 12-month term deposit rates across lenders.
positive.prompt: What is the highest 12-month term deposit rate in Australia right now?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls compare_rates with category term_deposit and termMonths 12 (customerSegment consumer if it chooses). Returns a ranked list of lenders and products, each with its rate and the date RateSonar recorded it. On 2026-10-17 the top row was 5.60% (recorded 2026-10-16). Rates change daily.

positive.description: Show one product's advertised rate history.
positive.prompt: How has CBA's Standard Variable Rate home loan for owner-occupiers changed since June 2026?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls find_products (institution CBA, query standard variable) to get institution_id cba and the product_id, then rate_history with both ids. Reports the recorded rate (6.49%, comparison rate 6.87% on 2026-10-17) with dates, and any change. It does not treat days with no record as observations.

positive.description: List recent home loan rate changes.
positive.prompt: Which lenders changed home loan rates in the last 7 days?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls rate_changes with category home_loan and sinceDays 7. Lists changes newest first with lender, product, old and new rate and the move in basis points (on 2026-10-17: Bank First +25 bps on 2026-10-16).

positive.description: Explain one product's bonus conditions from its published detail.
positive.prompt: What do I need to do to get the bonus rate on ING Savings Maximiser?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls find_products (institution ING, query savings maximiser), then rate_details with both ids. Gives the bonus rate (5.74% on 2026-10-17) and base rate (0.01%), the lender's own conditions, and the recorded date.

positive.description: Show a standard spread series against the RBA cash rate.
positive.prompt: How far above the RBA cash rate is CBA's variable home loan rate this month?
positive.expected_behavior: May call list_series to find the slug, then series with slugs [spread.hl.var-cash], institutions [cba] and median true. Reports the spread in basis points per day (179 bps on 2026-10-17), says the points are derived, and shows the market median. Without a key the window is the last 31 days.

negative.description: Personal financial advice. RateSonar reports advertised rates and has no advice tool. The assistant must not present a rate list as a recommendation for this person.
negative.prompt: I earn $120,000 and have a $600,000 loan. Which home loan should I switch to?
negative.expected_behavior: Does not recommend a product for the person. It may show recorded rates with their dates, and it says that a licensed adviser or broker can assess the person's situation.

negative.description: Application or account opening. RateSonar only reads data and has no write tools.
negative.prompt: Open an ING Savings Maximiser account for me.
negative.expected_behavior: Says it cannot open accounts or apply for products and sends the person to the lender's website. No RateSonar tool is expected to run.

negative.description: Outside coverage. RateSonar covers Australian lenders only.
negative.prompt: What are Kiwibank's home loan rates in New Zealand today?
negative.expected_behavior: Says RateSonar covers Australian lenders only and gives no New Zealand figure. If find_products runs, it returns no match and the assistant does not invent a rate.

review.commerce_description: RateSonar sells nothing in ChatGPT and processes no payments.

publication.release_notes: First release. Eleven read-only tools over RateSonar's dated record of advertised Australian rates and RBA market curves: find_products, compare_rates, rate_history, rate_details, rate_changes, list_series, series, bank_position, bank_analysis, yield_curve, curve_pipeline_status. No sign-in needed to start.
